description:
AstroCrew presents ARES PROTOCOL, a distributed engineering lab on Roblox (Luau) using custom N-body physics.

• Proposal: A public digital twin crowdsourcing human decision data to train NASA Artemis navigation AIs.

• Missions:

Mars: Base maintenance. • Europa: Subsurface ocean. • Earth: Carbon cleanup. • Moon: Farside radio & ice mining.

• Highlights: Real-time NASA DONKI solar data integration. • 100% procedural 3D scale & Luau orbital mechanics.
summary:
We developed an immersive, high-fidelity space simulator on the Roblox platform, powered by a completely custom physics engine. This includes realistic planetary gravity, orbital mechanics, inertia management, and 6DOF movement, seamlessly paired with cinematic audiovisuals. This project addresses the challenge by transforming complex concepts of astrophysics and spaceflight into an accessible, gamified learning experience for millions of young players globally.

This project is important because it serves a powerful dual purpose. First, it democratizes STEM education by sparking a genuine, hands-on interest in space exploration through intuitive gameplay rather than traditional textbooks. Second, the game acts as a massive crowdsourcing engine. By analyzing how thousands of players intuitively navigate general physics challenges—such as orbital insertions, managing momentum, and spacecraft docking—we generate valuable telemetry data. This crowdsourced human-behavior data has the potential to train NASA’s Machine Learning models, ultimately helping to improve autonomous navigation systems for future space exploration.
details:
What it does and how it works:

Note to judges: Our playable Alpha prototype is built in Roblox. We understand the platform requires an account to launch. Please refer primarily to our attached Slide Deck presentation to evaluate our complete concept, mission architecture, and how we integrated NASA data.

Our project is an immersive, gamified deep-space experience built on the massive Roblox platform. We have transformed a traditional gaming environment into a realistic zero-gravity physics simulator. Players are immersed in an environment where they must learn to navigate through space, master inertia, and perform orbital maneuvers, all through intuitive gameplay mechanics and cinematic-quality visuals that replicate the real-life experience of astronauts.

Intended impact and benefits: The impact of this project is twofold and highly scalable. First, for the players, it democratizes STEM education. It translates complex astrophysics and orbital mechanics concepts into kinesthetic learning (learning by doing). Users develop spatial problem-solving skills and spark a genuine interest in space exploration without needing to open a textbook. Within the game, players are directly rewarded for their precision and progress with unlockable spacecraft modules, mission badges, and exclusive access to an open-universe Sandbox mode upon completing the main campaign. Second, for space exploration and NASA, the game acts as a massive data crowdsourcing engine. By having thousands of players solve zero-gravity navigation challenges (such as docking spacecraft or stabilizing orbits), we can collect telemetry on their intuitive decisions. This immense database of human behavior in response to spatial problems can be used to train NASA Artificial Intelligence models, improving the autonomous navigation systems of future probes and spacecraft through Machine Learning.

Tools, coding languages, and software used: We used Roblox Studio and its Luau programming language as our base platform due to its massive global reach. We implemented advanced mathematical models for the physics simulation and integrated an immersive audiovisual design focused on replicating human perception in the vacuum of space.

How it is creative and factors considered: Our main creative innovation is using mass entertainment as a two-way bridge between science and society. We considered the enormous untapped potential of the Roblox user base (millions of active youth daily). Instead of creating a dry educational simulator, we designed a AAA experience where science and data collection happen in the background. Players have fun, earn in-game rewards, and compete, while seamlessly contributing to the advancement of spatial AI and shaping themselves into the next generation of engineers and innovators.
